GraphNodes.label: Compound Components
GraphNodes.description: Pattern for composition-plus-implicit-state UIs where parts share state without caller wiring

GraphNodes.label: Share state through context
GraphNodes.description: Using a context provider set by the parent and read by each subcomponent works at any nesting depth, unlike cloneElement prop injection

GraphNodes.label: Guard subcomponents
GraphNodes.description: Subcomponents throw a clear error when rendered outside their parent (e.g., <Tabs.Tab> must be used within <Tabs>)

GraphNodes.label: Accessibility spans the whole
GraphNodes.description: Roles, aria-controls/aria-selected wiring, and arrow-key handling live across all component parts together

GraphNodes.label: Namespace the parts
GraphNodes.description: Tabs.Tab (or co-located export) signals parts belong together and are typed as a set

GraphNodes.label: Controlled and Uncontrolled
GraphNodes.description: Two clean modes: uncontrolled (component owns value, caller seeds with defaultValue) or controlled (caller owns value via value+onChange)

GraphNodes.label: Two clean modes, never a hybrid
GraphNodes.description: A component that keeps its own state AND accepts value has two sources of truth that drift; switching modes causes framework warnings and cursor jumps

GraphNodes.label: defaultValue is mount-only
GraphNodes.description: Reading defaultValue on every render turns it into a second, broken value; read once to initialize, then component owns the value

GraphNodes.label: Controlled means obey
GraphNodes.description: In controlled mode, render exactly what value says and call onChange(next) when user asks for change — do not also apply the change locally

GraphNodes.label: Default to uncontrolled
GraphNodes.description: A plain text field does not need the parent to re-render on every keystroke; make the caller opt into controlled when value drives other UI or live validation

GraphNodes.label: Imperative handle stays small
GraphNodes.description: If a ref API is needed, expose focus(), reset(), scrollIntoView() — named, documented verbs, not the raw node or internal store

GraphNodes.label: The Props Contract
GraphNodes.description: Rules for designing stable, permanent, and intentional prop APIs

GraphNodes.label: Every prop is permanent
GraphNodes.description: Once a consumer uses a prop, removing or changing it is a breaking change; it's also a test case, docs line, and maintenance branch

GraphNodes.label: Make illegal states unrepresentable
GraphNodes.description: Use unions (e.g., variant) instead of multiple booleans that allow nonsensical combinations and need precedence rules

GraphNodes.label: Name for intent, consistently
GraphNodes.description: Handlers follow framework event convention (on<Event> in React); booleans read as state (disabled, not enabled={false}); same concept has same name across library

GraphNodes.label: Do not leak internals
GraphNodes.description: A prop typed as the component's private internal model couples every caller to a shape that should be free to change; export a deliberate public type instead

GraphNodes.label: No god object
GraphNodes.description: A single config={...} prop is an untyped, un-discoverable API; use real named props with defaults for the common case

GraphNodes.label: Slots vs Configuration Props
GraphNodes.description: Rules for deciding when to use slots (caller provides markup) vs props (component decides markup from value)

GraphNodes.label: Config props do not scale to structure
GraphNodes.description: Every new layout need adds a prop (showFooter, headerActions, leftIcon, etc.), making render a maze of conditionals — closed for extension

GraphNodes.label: Slots invert that
GraphNodes.description: children and named slots let the caller supply the markup; component owns behaviour and wiring, caller owns content

GraphNodes.label: Use slot when caller provides markup/subtree
GraphNodes.description: Use a slot when the caller provides markup or a subtree; use a prop when the component decides the markup from a value (variant, count, status)

GraphNodes.label: Expose state through the slot
GraphNodes.description: A render prop or scoped slot passes a small, typed, stable argument (e.g., { isOpen, close }) — not the whole internal state object

GraphNodes.label: Name slots by role
GraphNodes.description: Name slots by role that stay meaningful as uses change (header, actions, empty), not dashboardHeaderSlot

GraphNodes.label: Versioning a Shared Component
GraphNodes.description: Rules for backward-compatible API changes over time

GraphNodes.label: API is bigger than the props type
GraphNodes.description: Consumers depend on prop names, default values, rendered DOM structure, and class/slot names they style/query against; any changing under them is a breaking change

GraphNodes.label: Deprecate, do not delete
GraphNodes.description: A prop being renamed keeps working for one major version: accept both, map old to new, mark @deprecated with replacement, warn once in development

GraphNodes.label: Defaults are frozen
GraphNodes.description: Changing a default (e.g., size from md to sm) silently restyles every existing usage — that is a major change with migration note, never a minor

GraphNodes.label: Renames ship a codemod
GraphNodes.description: A find-and-replace the consumer runs, plus a changelog entry with version and before/after
